subject: Follow-up: Competitive eval & model-quality tests (Redwood vs hyperscalers)
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@atlasanalytics.com>, Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@atlasanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 15:02:00 +0000
Subject: Follow-up: Competitive eval & model-quality tests (Redwood vs hyperscalers)

Hi Emma / Marcus,

Thanks again for the call earlier — great to meet you both. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum on the competitive evaluation: 

What we agreed:
- Redwood will run a focused model-quality comparison across the prompt set you shared (customer support + knowledge retrieval prompts) against the provider models you flagged (OpenAI / Anthropic / AWS Bedrock).
- Primary metrics: hallucination/factuality rate (per prompt), exact-match / F1 where applicable, and qualitative regression checks on safety/factuality.
- Secondary metrics: median latency and estimated cost-per-1k tokens for typical request sizes.

Deliverables (proposed):
1) CSV with per-prompt scores and labels (hallucination flag, confidence).
2) Short write-up of notable regressions and example failures.
3) Side-by-side latency/cost table and recommended next tests (e.g., reranking, prefix caching).

Timeline: we can run the initial batch and share results by end of week (EOW Fri, Mar 13) if you provide the final prompt set and one or two representative KB/context examples.

Attachments: redwood_eval_plan.pdf (test plan), eval_prompts.csv (sample prompt set), eval_config.yaml (run config).

Questions for you:
- Can you confirm the final prompt CSV (we used the sample you sent in the call notes) and provide 3 representative knowledge snippets (size ~500-1k tokens) you care most about?
- Any hard constraints we should know about (e.g., max acceptable hallucination rate, latency SLO)?

Once I have those we’ll loop Rishi (SE) to run the comparisons and share raw outputs + a short slide summary.

Thanks — Neha

--
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0192
From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@atlasanalytics.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@atlasanalytics.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 18:27:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Competitive eval & model-quality tests (Redwood vs hyperscalers)

Hi Neha — thanks for the summary and the plan. That timeline works for us. A few clarifications from our side: 

- We’ll upload the finalized prompt CSV to the Drive link you shared by EOD today.
- Priority metrics: hallucination/factuality is most important. For our scoring we typically treat any unsupported assertion about the customer KB as a hallucination. A target we’re evaluating against is <= 5% hallucination on the seed prompts, but we’re open to seeing baseline results first.
- Models to include in the comparison: Redwood-instruct-v2 (or closest production variant you recommend), Redwood-quant-2 (if available), OpenAI gpt-4o, Anthropic Claude-instant, and AWS Bedrock's selected model. If there are Redwood-specific variants you think matter for cost/latency tradeoffs, include those.

Two asks:
1) Can you add a short section in the deliverable showing example prompts where Redwood differs from the hyperscalers (good and bad) so our PM can triage?
2) Please surface any preprocessing or prompt templating you use so we can replicate locally.

We’ll also share one representative KB chunk and a small set of recent tickets to use as context. Thanks — Emma

--
Emma Jones
Head of Product, Search & Knowledge | Atlas Analytics
emma.jones@atlasanalytics.com
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 02:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Competitive eval & model-quality tests (Redwood vs hyperscalers)

Thanks Neha — looping in plan from the SE side. Based on Emma’s asks I’ll run the following: 

Planned test harness:
- Use the provided prompt CSV + KB snippets. For contextual prompts we’ll truncate/align tokens consistently and log effective context size.
- Models: redwood-instruct-v2, redwood-quant-2, openai-gpt-4o, anthropic-claude-instant, aws-bedrock-default (we’ll use their most comparable generation config).
- Metrics:
  * Hallucination/factuality: human-label a stratified sample (50 prompts) and run the factuality classifier for the full set.
  * Exact-match / F1 for structured QA prompts.
  * Safety/abuse flags: run Redwood safety filters + record rate of mitigations.
  * Latency: p50/p95 measured on 1000 requests with representative token sizes.
  * Estimated cost: use public pricing + token counts to compute cost-per-1k.

Deliverables and format:
- results_per_prompt.csv (per-model columns: score, hallucination_flag, notes)
- failures_examples.md (annotated examples)
- run_logs.tar.gz (artifacts and config)

I’ll use the eval_config.yaml attached (includes model temperature, top_p, max_tokens, and batching settings). If Atlas has any different temperature suggestions, let me know.

Schedule: start now (once prompts and KB arrive) — share an internal draft by EOD Thu (Mar 12) and a cleaned slide + CSV by Fri (Mar 13). If we see obvious regressions we’ll call out quick mitigations (prompt template tweaks or reranking).

- Rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@atlasanalytics.com>, Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@atlasanalytics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Competitive eval & model-quality tests (Redwood vs hyperscalers)

Emma / Marcus — perfect, thanks for the confirmations. We’ve received the prompt CSV in Drive and Rishi’s started the runs. Couple of quick notes: 

- HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.example.com/deal/RDW-2026-0142 (I’ve added the evaluation milestones and owner).
- If the initial results are promising we’d propose a short follow-up demo week of Mar 23–25 to go over examples and discuss productionization options (dedicated capacity vs hosted API + caching).
- For procurement track: our standard POC credits and a small evaluation discount are available — we’ll surface pricing once we have a sense of throughput/cost.

Next steps for Atlas:
1) Confirm any temperature/top_p changes (default: temp=0.0, top_p=0.95).
2) Share any extra KB snippets you want included by EOD today.

Rishi / Marissa — I’ll watch for the draft on Thu and we’ll prep the slide deck for Friday.

Thanks — Neha

--
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
